runs.text: Leverage has risen and its level depends on the EBITDA basis. Total debt of USD 2,456.5 million at September 26, 2026 compares with USD 2,152.2 million at FY2025, so total debt to EBITDA before impairment lines moved from 2.68x to 3.00x and net debt to the same EBITDA from 2.41x to 2.75x [CP-1]. Unadjusted for the Q4 2025 goodwill and intangible impairments of USD 376.0 million, the ratios are 5.02x and 5.53x. The impairments are non-cash and fall entirely in Q4 2025, which is why the adjusted basis is the primary view, but the lender definition is unknown. Covenant-compliant status at FY2025 with an unadjusted 5.02x against a 4.25x ceiling implies that covenant EBITDA adds back impairments or other items; this is an inference, not a verified fact.

Interest burden is light. Cash paid for interest was USD 102.8 million over the LTM against EBITDA before impairment lines of USD 819.9 million (7.97x; 4.32x unadjusted) [CP-1]. Three note series carry fixed coupons of 3.75% to 4.25%, and the weighted average rate on all debt was 4.11%. The floating-rate revolver of USD 943.2 million is 38.4% of total debt (C5), and the 10-K reports no swap after the fiscal 2024 swap matured, so the revolver is an unhedged rate exposure; an illustrative 100 bp move would change annual interest by about USD 9.4 million (C5).

Liquidity is adequate and the maturity profile is back-ended. Cash of USD 200.4 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,056.8 million gives about USD 1,257.2 million before letters of credit of USD 21.7 million (C1). The revolver matures in December 2029; the last annual table shows USD 1.3 million and USD 1.5 million maturing in FY2026 and FY2027 and USD 501.3 million in FY2028 [CP-1]. The USD 2,120.3 million across FY2028 to FY2030 is concentrated in one window, and the larger revolver draw moves more of it into FY2029.

Cash conversion funds operations but not the 2026 programme. LTM free cash flow of USD 399.6 million is below FY2025's USD 518.5 million [CP-1]. In nine months 2026 acquisitions of USD 467.3 million and treasury stock of USD 324.1 million, together USD 791.4 million, exceeded free cash flow of USD 341.1 million by USD 450.3 million (C2); sale proceeds of USD 176.6 million and USD 58.1 million from surrendered life insurance policies offset part, and the revolver rose USD 326.7 million. The mechanism is shareholder returns and M&A outrunning internal cash generation, so leverage tolerance is a management choice, and the pages read set no leverage target [CP-1A].

Covenant headroom cannot be confirmed. The revolver carries a minimum 3.50x test of EBITDA less capital expenditures to cash interest and a maximum 4.25x test of indebtedness to EBITDA, and the issuer stated compliance only at December 27, 2025 [CP-1]. On this handoff's definitions the cover measure is 5.81x and leverage 3.00x for the LTM, which look comfortable, but the covenant definitions differ and are not in the pack, so no 2026 headroom can be calculated.

Business risk is moderate and backlog-supported. No client exceeded 4% of FY2025 revenue, DSA backlog was USD 2.0 billion at September 26, 2026 against USD 1.9 billion at FY2025, and DSA revenue is recognized over time as work is performed [CP-1A]. The risks are client funding and study cancellations, which carry no termination fee in many contracts, and the animal-sourcing exposure that led to government investigations now closed [CP-1A]. A securities class action is pending with no loss estimate.

Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden. Operating lease liabilities were USD 491.7 million at FY2025, unconditional purchase obligations about USD 340 million, contingent consideration USD 45.0 million, unfunded venture capital commitments about USD 49.4 million (C3), and the issuer may fund up to USD 45.0 million of the divested CDMO businesses' losses and capital spending [CP-1, CP-1A]. None is in the debt total.

Earnings quality needs care. LTM EBITDA is calculated from operating income and cash flow D&A, includes the divested businesses up to May 2026, and includes a USD 38.5 million gain on the Wilmington site sale in nine months 2026 [CP-1]. Management savings targets are claims, not results [CP-1A]. Q3 2026 net income includes a large tax benefit and is not an operating measure.

cells.text: Three reportable segments: RMS (research models and services), DSA (discovery and safety assessment, outsourced regulated testing) and Manufacturing (biologics testing and related solutions, and until May 2026 CDMO services); the CDMO and Cell Solutions businesses were sold in May 2026

runs.text: Strengths. (1) Diversified customer base with no client above 4% of FY2025 revenue and DSA backlog of USD 2.0 billion [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. (2) High interest cover of 7.97x on EBITDA before impairment lines and a majority of debt in low-coupon fixed-rate notes [Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the ratio basis, CP-1]. (3) Large undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,056.8 million with maturity in December 2029 and little principal due before FY2028 [Documentary Fact, CP-1]. (4) Positive free cash flow of USD 399.6 million over the LTM [Documentary Fact inputs, calculated, CP-1]. (5) Resolution of the DOJ and SEC investigations in 2025 removes a legal overhang [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

Weaknesses. (1) Leverage rose to 3.00x on the primary basis and is 5.53x unadjusted, with covenant EBITDA unverified [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1]. (2) Capital allocation favors acquisitions and buybacks funded partly by the revolver, and debt repayment is listed among several uses without a target [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. (3) The revolver is floating-rate and unhedged on the 10-K evidence, and the FY2028 to FY2030 maturities are concentrated [Documentary Fact, CP-1]. (4) Earnings carry restructuring charges of USD 73.8 million in nine months 2026, large impairments in Q4 2025, and pending savings claims [Documentary Fact and Management Language, CP-1A]. (5) The legal structure is unknown: guarantors, security of the notes and covenant definitions are Insufficient Information because the agreements are not supplied [CP-0].

runs.text: No new debt issue, refinancing or credit agreement amendment is described in the sources for fiscal 2026. The debt note shows the same revolver and three note series at September 26, 2026 as at December 27, 2025, with a larger revolver balance (Q3 10-Q page:25). The transactions below are acquisitions and disposals, not financings.

Cambodian NHP Supplier. On January 14, 2026 the issuer acquired certain assets of K.F. Cambodia Ltd for a preliminary purchase price of 507.3 million, of which 335.0 million was paid at closing and 172.3 million is deferred consideration payable on post-close conditions. The issuer paid 100.0 million of deferred consideration in Q3 2026 and 170.0 million in nine months 2026, with the remaining balance stated as 5 million. It was funded by cash and the Credit Facility and is reported in DSA and RMS (Q3 10-Q pages 13, 36, 48). Status: completed. The Q3 10-Q describes the acquired NHPs as vertically integrated into the DSA supply chain or sold to third-party clients through RMS.

PathoQuest SAS. On April 17, 2026 the issuer acquired an additional 79% equity interest for 67.4 million, funded by cash and the Credit Facility, and it now holds 100% (Q3 10-Q pages 13, 36). It is reported in Manufacturing. Status: completed.

Wilmington site. In March 2026 the issuer sold buildings for 60.1 million net of costs, recognized a pre-tax gain of 38.5 million, and entered a long-term operating lease for certain buildings (Q3 10-Q page:23). The creditor effect is cash in and a new lease claim outside debt.

European Discovery Services sale. Signed February 25, 2026 at 145.0 million in cash plus up to 10.0 million of contingent payments (Q1 10-Q page:14); closed May 22, 2026 to IQVIA Inc. at a preliminary 125.2 million net of costs to sell (Q2 10-Q page:15), later stated as 126.4 million net of costs (Q3 10-Q page:16). The contingent payments are valued at 2.8 million. Status: completed. The three headline figures are logged in Conflicts below.

CDMO and Cell Solutions sale. Completed May 6, 2026 to GI Partners. The issuer paid net cash of 12.4 million to the buyer, may fund up to 45.0 million of future EBITDA losses and capital expenditures of the divested businesses over four years, and may receive up to 50.0 million of contingent payments valued at 15.7 million. Pre-tax losses were 118.0 million in Q1 2026 and 63.7 million in Q2 2026, totaling 181.7 million for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16; Q1 10-Q page:14). Status: completed; the funding obligation is a contingent claim outside reported debt.

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect: nine-month 2026 sale proceeds of 176,563 thousand and a further 58,127 thousand from surrendered life insurance policies (Q3 10-Q page:7) were outweighed by 467,254 thousand for acquisitions and 324,105 thousand for treasury stock, and the revolver rose by 326,671 thousand (CP-1 handoff). No transaction document is supplied, so sponsor, guarantor or lender consent terms are Insufficient Information.

Reporting currency: USD. Current period: Q3 2026 (quarter ended September 26, 2026); prior period: FY2025 (fiscal year ended December 27, 2025). The sources print amounts in thousands of US dollars (the releases also use millions in text); statement tables below are in US$ thousands as printed, and the four chart tables are in US$m or x as their headers require.

fields.value: Scope: reported FY2024 and FY2025 statements, the Q3 2026 and nine-month 2026 interim statements, a last-twelve-months (LTM) build to September 26, 2026, the debt register, liquidity, covenant terms and claims outside the debt figure. Out of scope: ratings, forecasts, valuation, pro forma adjustments for the May 2026 divestitures and 2026 acquisitions. The entity is the registrant on a consolidated basis; the context names no borrower, parent or guarantor.

fields.value: Locators are written as page:N of the named source, where a page is the extracted chunk, not the printed page. "10-K" is the FY2025 annual report, "Q3 10-Q" the quarter ended September 26, 2026, and "Q3 release" the November 4, 2026 Exhibit 99.1.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The financial base is usable for the downstream credit work, with stated limits. Reported statements for FY2024, FY2025, Q3 2026 and nine months 2026 are extracted from the filings and agree internally where checked. Because the issuer reports no EBITDA, this handoff calculates EBITDA as operating income plus depreciation and amortization from the cash flow statement, and also shows it before the two separately printed impairment lines (goodwill and intangible asset). The second form is used in the chart tables because the impairments are non-cash and sit entirely in Q4 2025; the unadjusted ratios are shown alongside and are materially higher.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage on the chosen basis is moderate and has risen since year-end, because debt grew faster than the LTM earnings base. Cash interest cover is high on both bases. The main limits are that LTM mixes pre-divestiture and post-divestiture periods without pro forma adjustment, that covenant EBITDA and indebtedness are defined in a credit agreement that is not in the pack, and that the revolver's availability net of letters of credit is not stated. Nothing in this handoff is a covenant calculation or a rating view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: How to read the leverage basis: the unadjusted ratios treat the Q4 2025 impairments as if they reduced earnings capacity and are shown only because the company does not report EBITDA. They are not covenant ratios. The covenant definitions are not in the pack, so which basis the lenders use cannot be confirmed (see Covenants).

Q3 depreciation and amortization from the Q3 release (page:13) is 72,260 thousand (2026) and 85,164 thousand (2025).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The weighted average interest rate on the debt was 4.11% at September 26, 2026 and 4.05% at December 27, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:26). Book and fair value of the Senior Notes at September 26, 2026 are 500,000 and 488,500 (2028 notes), 500,000 and 473,450 (2029 notes), and 500,000 and 456,250 (2031 notes), all below book (Q3 10-Q page:24). Letters of credit outstanding were 21.7 million at September 26, 2026 (Q3 10-Q pages 26, 49). The 10-K says the interest rate swap on revolver borrowings matured in fiscal 2024 and no further swap contracts had been entered (10-K page:108); the Q3 10-Q does not restate this, so revolver interest is treated as unhedged on the evidence available.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The 10-K states two maintenance covenants under the revolving credit facility, tested over four consecutive fiscal quarters: consolidated EBITDA less capital expenditures to consolidated cash interest expense of no less than 3.50 to 1.0, and consolidated indebtedness plus principal outstanding under permitted receivables financing to consolidated EBITDA of no more than 4.25 to 1.0. The Company stated it was compliant with all financial covenants at December 27, 2025 (10-K page:152). No 2026 compliance statement or covenant figure was found (CP-0 gap, confirmed).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Indicative comparison only, on this handoff's definitions (C8): EBITDA before impairment lines less capex over cash interest is 5.75x for FY2025 and 5.81x for LTM Q3 2026 against the 3.50x floor, and total debt over EBITDA before impairment lines is 2.68x and 3.00x against the 4.25x ceiling. The covenant definitions of EBITDA and indebtedness differ from these calculations and are not in the pack. On unadjusted EBITDA, FY2025 leverage of 5.02x would exceed 4.25x while the Company reported compliance, so the covenant EBITDA must add back impairments or other items (inference from the two printed facts, not verified).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Q3 2026: revenue of 982,732 thousand fell from 1,004,852 thousand in Q3 2025, and operating income rose from 133,799 to 202,638 thousand (Q3 10-Q page:5). The quarter included the 100.0 million deferred payment for the Cambodian NHP Supplier (Q3 10-Q page:48). No new debt issuance or facility amendment in the quarter was found; the debt note shows only a larger revolver balance. At September 26, 2026, 700.0 million remained on the 1.0 billion repurchase authorization (Q3 10-Q page:27), which is capacity for further buybacks. After the quarter end and before the cutoff: the Company filed a motion to dismiss the second amended complaint in the securities class action on October 15, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:52), and the Q3 10-Q and release are dated November 4, 2026. No post-quarter financing event was found.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage. Total debt rose by 304,279 thousand between FY2025 and September 26, 2026 (C9). The 10-Q cites net proceeds of 339.0 million, primarily from the Credit Facility, and nine-month cash uses of 467,254 thousand for acquisitions, 324,105 thousand for treasury stock and 111,394 thousand for contingent and deferred consideration, partly offset by 176,563 thousand of sale proceeds (Q3 10-Q pages 7, 48). The mechanism is borrowing under the Credit Facility while acquisition, buyback and deferred-consideration outflows exceeded free cash flow, which lifts leverage on a flat earnings base. EBITDA before impairment lines rose only from 804,448 to 819,935 thousand over the same comparison.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Coverage and cash flow. Cash interest cover is high, because the three note series carry coupons of 3.75% to 4.25% and the weighted average rate on all debt is 4.11%. Free cash flow for the nine months was 341,064 thousand (C4) against 324,105 thousand of treasury stock purchases, so buybacks absorbed nearly all of it. Operating cash flow fell from 590,126 to 474,887 thousand between the two nine-month periods; the 10-Q attributes this to higher variable compensation payments and professional fees (Q3 10-Q page:46).

Pathway: credit snapshot; reporting currency USD; current period Q3 2026, prior period FY2025. The reader question is which transaction, ownership, business and operating facts matter most to a creditor. The review gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion. Figures are copied from the cited pages or from the CP-1 handoff and are not recomputed here except where stated in Calculations.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer is a publicly listed research and testing company with no sponsor, and its creditor-relevant story is a portfolio reshaping. After a 2025 Cooperation Agreement with a large shareholder, the board ran a strategic review that ended in November 2025 with a plan to focus on core scientific services, divest non-core assets and allocate capital across acquisitions, buybacks and debt repayment. In 2026 the issuer executed that plan: it bought the Cambodian NHP Supplier and the rest of PathoQuest, and sold its CDMO, Cell Solutions and certain European Discovery businesses. The operating model is anchored in regulated safety testing and research models for biopharma clients with no concentration above 4% of revenue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: For creditors the mechanism is that the sales and the cost programmes aim to lift margin, while acquisitions, deferred payments and buybacks consume cash and the revolver funded the gap, taking total debt from 2,152,221 thousand to 2,456,500 thousand. Governance evidence is mixed: the buyback authorization and the shareholder agreement point to equity-friendly allocation, but the sources show no controlling owner, no related-party leakage and no creditor-adverse action; buybacks are ordinary shareholder returns. Willingness to delever is not documented. Legal capacity under the credit agreement and indentures cannot be assessed because they are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt issue, refinancing or credit agreement amendment is described in the sources for fiscal 2026. The debt note shows the same revolver and three note series at September 26, 2026 as at December 27, 2025, with a larger revolver balance (Q3 10-Q page:25). The transactions below are acquisitions and disposals, not financings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cambodian NHP Supplier. On January 14, 2026 the issuer acquired certain assets of K.F. Cambodia Ltd for a preliminary purchase price of 507.3 million, of which 335.0 million was paid at closing and 172.3 million is deferred consideration payable on post-close conditions. The issuer paid 100.0 million of deferred consideration in Q3 2026 and 170.0 million in nine months 2026, with the remaining balance stated as 5 million. It was funded by cash and the Credit Facility and is reported in DSA and RMS (Q3 10-Q pages 13, 36, 48). Status: completed. The Q3 10-Q describes the acquired NHPs as vertically integrated into the DSA supply chain or sold to third-party clients through RMS.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PathoQuest SAS. On April 17, 2026 the issuer acquired an additional 79% equity interest for 67.4 million, funded by cash and the Credit Facility, and it now holds 100% (Q3 10-Q pages 13, 36). It is reported in Manufacturing. Status: completed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Wilmington site. In March 2026 the issuer sold buildings for 60.1 million net of costs, recognized a pre-tax gain of 38.5 million, and entered a long-term operating lease for certain buildings (Q3 10-Q page:23). The creditor effect is cash in and a new lease claim outside debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: European Discovery Services sale. Signed February 25, 2026 at 145.0 million in cash plus up to 10.0 million of contingent payments (Q1 10-Q page:14); closed May 22, 2026 to IQVIA Inc. at a preliminary 125.2 million net of costs to sell (Q2 10-Q page:15), later stated as 126.4 million net of costs (Q3 10-Q page:16). The contingent payments are valued at 2.8 million. Status: completed. The three headline figures are logged in Conflicts below.

fields.value: CDMO and Cell Solutions sale. Completed May 6, 2026 to GI Partners. The issuer paid net cash of 12.4 million to the buyer, may fund up to 45.0 million of future EBITDA losses and capital expenditures of the divested businesses over four years, and may receive up to 50.0 million of contingent payments valued at 15.7 million. Pre-tax losses were 118.0 million in Q1 2026 and 63.7 million in Q2 2026, totaling 181.7 million for nine months 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16; Q1 10-Q page:14). Status: completed; the funding obligation is a contingent claim outside reported debt.

No transaction document is supplied, so sponsor, guarantor or lender consent terms are Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability. Evidence: no client above 4% of FY2025 revenue (10-K page:26) and DSA backlog of 2.0 billion at September 26, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:35). Mechanism: spread clients and a backlog worked off over varying durations reduce dependence on any one contract, but termination without fees is possible (10-K page:43). Implication: debt service is supported by diversified, contracted cash flows; a sharp biotech funding downturn is the main swing factor. The counter-evidence is that Q3 2026 revenue fell year over year, driven by the May 2026 divestitures (Q3 release page:2).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: cost programmes of about 300 million of annualized savings by the end of 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:36) against restructuring charges of 73.8 million in nine months 2026. Mechanism: savings flow to margin only if volumes hold, and charges consume cash first. Implication: EBITDA expansion is partly management-claimed and not yet reflected in cash conversion (CP-1 shows lower LTM free cash flow than FY2025).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation. Evidence: 324,105 thousand of buybacks and 467,254 thousand of acquisitions in nine months 2026 with the revolver up by 326,671 thousand. Mechanism: shareholder returns and M&A are funded partly from the revolver, lifting leverage to 3.00x on the CP-1 basis from 2.68x. Implication: leverage tolerance is a policy choice; the 10-K lists debt repayment as one of several uses without a target (10-K page:25). Willingness to reduce debt is Insufficient Information.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Concentration and supply. Evidence: the DOJ and SEC investigations of NHP shipments are closed (10-K page:91) and the Cambodian supplier was acquired (Q3 10-Q page:13). Mechanism: owning an NHP source can reduce third-party supply risk but concentrates a regulated animal-sourcing exposure in the DSA and RMS chain. Implication: an unfavourable sourcing event would hit DSA volumes; no current evidence of one.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for CHARLES RIVER LABORATORIES INTERNATIONAL, INC. (issuer id crl), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit snapshot, reporting currency USD. It draws on the CP-1 financial base and the CP-1A business and transaction context, with no new source text. It gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Locators are page:N of the named source; the CP-1 and CP-1A tables carry them for each fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Charles River Laboratories is a moderately leveraged but cash-generative research and testing company whose credit is sound yet weakening on leverage. Its strongest support is diversified, backlog-backed demand: no client above 4% of FY2025 revenue, a DSA backlog of USD 2.0 billion, and EBITDA before impairment lines covering cash interest 7.97x. Its weakest point is capital allocation: total debt rose to USD 2,456.5 million and leverage to 3.00x as borrowing under the revolver accompanied acquisitions and buybacks on a broadly flat earnings base. The outcome depends on whether free cash flow and divestiture proceeds go to debt reduction rather than further buybacks, and on whether covenant EBITDA, which is not defined in the pack, leaves room under the 4.25x ceiling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage has risen and its level depends on the EBITDA basis. Total debt of USD 2,456.5 million at September 26, 2026 compares with USD 2,152.2 million at FY2025, so total debt to EBITDA before impairment lines moved from 2.68x to 3.00x and net debt to the same EBITDA from 2.41x to 2.75x [CP-1]. Unadjusted for the Q4 2025 goodwill and intangible impairments of USD 376.0 million, the ratios are 5.02x and 5.53x. The impairments are non-cash and fall entirely in Q4 2025, which is why the adjusted basis is the primary view, but the lender definition is unknown. Covenant-compliant status at FY2025 with an unadjusted 5.02x against a 4.25x ceiling implies that covenant EBITDA adds back impairments or other items; this is an inference, not a verified fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest burden is light. Cash paid for interest was USD 102.8 million over the LTM against EBITDA before impairment lines of USD 819.9 million (7.97x; 4.32x unadjusted) [CP-1]. Three note series carry fixed coupons of 3.75% to 4.25%, and the weighted average rate on all debt was 4.11%. The floating-rate revolver of USD 943.2 million is 38.4% of total debt (C5), and the 10-K reports no swap after the fiscal 2024 swap matured, so the revolver is an unhedged rate exposure; an illustrative 100 bp move would change annual interest by about USD 9.4 million (C5).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and the maturity profile is back-ended. Cash of USD 200.4 million plus undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,056.8 million gives about USD 1,257.2 million before letters of credit of USD 21.7 million (C1). The revolver matures in December 2029; the last annual table shows USD 1.3 million and USD 1.5 million maturing in FY2026 and FY2027 and USD 501.3 million in FY2028 [CP-1]. The USD 2,120.3 million across FY2028 to FY2030 is concentrated in one window, and the larger revolver draw moves more of it into FY2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion funds operations but not the 2026 programme. LTM free cash flow of USD 399.6 million is below FY2025's USD 518.5 million [CP-1]. In nine months 2026 acquisitions of USD 467.3 million and treasury stock of USD 324.1 million, together USD 791.4 million, exceeded free cash flow of USD 341.1 million by USD 450.3 million (C2); sale proceeds of USD 176.6 million and USD 58.1 million from surrendered life insurance policies offset part, and the revolver rose USD 326.7 million. The mechanism is shareholder returns and M&A outrunning internal cash generation, so leverage tolerance is a management choice, and the pages read set no leverage target [CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom cannot be confirmed. The revolver carries a minimum 3.50x test of EBITDA less capital expenditures to cash interest and a maximum 4.25x test of indebtedness to EBITDA, and the issuer stated compliance only at December 27, 2025 [CP-1]. On this handoff's definitions the cover measure is 5.81x and leverage 3.00x for the LTM, which look comfortable, but the covenant definitions differ and are not in the pack, so no 2026 headroom can be calculated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is moderate and backlog-supported. No client exceeded 4% of FY2025 revenue, DSA backlog was USD 2.0 billion at September 26, 2026 against USD 1.9 billion at FY2025, and DSA revenue is recognized over time as work is performed [CP-1A]. The risks are client funding and study cancellations, which carry no termination fee in many contracts, and the animal-sourcing exposure that led to government investigations now closed [CP-1A]. A securities class action is pending with no loss estimate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden. Operating lease liabilities were USD 491.7 million at FY2025, unconditional purchase obligations about USD 340 million, contingent consideration USD 45.0 million, unfunded venture capital commitments about USD 49.4 million (C3), and the issuer may fund up to USD 45.0 million of the divested CDMO businesses' losses and capital spending [CP-1, CP-1A]. None is in the debt total.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality needs care. LTM EBITDA is calculated from operating income and cash flow D&A, includes the divested businesses up to May 2026, and includes a USD 38.5 million gain on the Wilmington site sale in nine months 2026 [CP-1]. Management savings targets are claims, not results [CP-1A]. Q3 2026 net income includes a large tax benefit and is not an operating measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. (1) Diversified customer base with no client above 4% of FY2025 revenue and DSA backlog of USD 2.0 billion [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. (2) High interest cover of 7.97x on EBITDA before impairment lines and a majority of debt in low-coupon fixed-rate notes [Documentary Fact for the inputs, Analyst Interpretation for the ratio basis, CP-1]. (3) Large undrawn revolver capacity of USD 1,056.8 million with maturity in December 2029 and little principal due before FY2028 [Documentary Fact, CP-1]. (4) Positive free cash flow of USD 399.6 million over the LTM [Documentary Fact inputs, calculated, CP-1]. (5) Resolution of the DOJ and SEC investigations in 2025 removes a legal overhang [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. (1) Leverage rose to 3.00x on the primary basis and is 5.53x unadjusted, with covenant EBITDA unverified [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1]. (2) Capital allocation favors acquisitions and buybacks funded partly by the revolver, and debt repayment is listed among several uses without a target [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. (3) The revolver is floating-rate and unhedged on the 10-K evidence, and the FY2028 to FY2030 maturities are concentrated [Documentary Fact, CP-1]. (4) Earnings carry restructuring charges of USD 73.8 million in nine months 2026, large impairments in Q4 2025, and pending savings claims [Documentary Fact and Management Language, CP-1A]. (5) The legal structure is unknown: guarantors, security of the notes and covenant definitions are Insufficient Information because the agreements are not supplied [CP-0].
